text:
maria_sales: Quick sync: Eli from Polarus wants a Private/VPC POC. They prefer PrivateLink but may fallback to peering. Need a short, copy-paste checklist and exact items we need from them.

jia_se: Copy. I'll draft the checklist. Main decision points: PrivateLink vs Peering, hosted API key for dev smoke tests vs Dedicated egress IPs, and whether they want Private DNS enabled.

jia_se: Minimal customer checklist (send to customer):
```
- VPC ID and account ID for the POC VPC
- Primary CIDR block (eg 10.50.0.0/16) and confirmation there's no overlap with Redwood ranges
- Subnet IDs (one per AZ) to place interface endpoints (PrivateLink) or to route to (peering)
- Route table IDs to update for each AZ (if peering)
- Security group for the endpoint with outbound HTTPS (443) and inbound from your app if you want private DNS resolved
- Contact person for VPCE creation and a Slack handle for rapid troubleshooting
```

omar_netops: For PrivateLink, we need the VPCE security group id and the subnet IDs where the interface ENIs will land. We will provide the service name and accept the endpoint after creation. For peering, provide the peer request with vpc-id, owner-id, and desired route tables.

ben_infra: Notes on DNS & routes:
- If you enable private DNS for the endpoint, calls to our service host will resolve to the VPCE private IPs automatically. If you don't want that, leave it disabled and use the explicit host we give.
- TGW customers: provide the attachment ID and confirm you allow explicit routes to the ENI subnets. Peering + TGW needs explicit routes on spoke RTs.

eli_customer: We plan to use a single VPC in us-east-1, CIDR 10.60.0.0/16. We prefer not to touch private DNS because we have internal hostnames collisions. Also we want a 7-day temp API key for our engineers. Can you accept VPCEs within 6 hours?

maria_sales: Yes we can accept within that window. We will create the service in us-east-1 and share the exact service name. Temp hosted API key for 7 days is OK; we issue scoped keys for POCs.

omar_netops: Additional security checklist to tell their firewall team:
```
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to our VPCE private IPs (we'll share after acceptance)
- Allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to your resolver if you want to resolve private DNS names
- If peering: add route to our peer CIDR with the peering connection id we provide
```

ben_infra: For Dedicated pools option: we can give a list of static egress IPs for the pool. If they want requests to originate from their VPC (no egress to our public endpoints) they'd need a Private deployment. Clarify which they want.

jia_se: Also confirm if they need audit logs of the VPCE acceptance and whether they'd like CloudTrail export to their S3. We can export acceptance events and service usage logs on Private deployments.

oncall-bot: Ticket NET-6121 opened for Polarus POC network onboarding. Assignee: omar_netops. Priority: P2.

eli_customer: I'll create the VPCE today and share the ID here. We won't enable private DNS for now. Please send the temp API key to dev@polarus.com when ready.

maria_sales: Will do. Next actions for our team:
- Create endpoint service in us-east-1 and send service name to Eli
- Prepare 7-day hosted API key and email to dev@polarus.com
- If they choose Dedicated, prepare egress IP list
- Accept VPCE and confirm SG & DNS behavior within 6 hours of creation

omar_netops: FYI for internal: subnet sizing /24 per AZ, avoid 10.60.0.0/20 overlaps with our test pool (172.31.200.0/22). If they opt for peering, remind them peering is non-transitive.

maria_sales: Scheduling 20-min handoff with Polarus for tomorrow 11am ET to walk through the checklist and confirm VPCE creation flow. I'll include jia, omar, ben. Thanks all :thumbsup:
